steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain, cool, and chop.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, mayonnaise, sweet pickle relish, sugar, onion, mustard, vinegar, celery, pimentos, carrot, parsley, pepper, and salt. Mix well, chill and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Restaurant-Style Potato Salad
raw_recipe.description: Parsley, shredded carrot, pimentos and white onion all play their part in making the dressing and the salad taste sensational in this russet potato salad recipe.

video.description: In this video, we'll share with you a restaurant-worthy potato salad. It is ready in under an hour and has ingredients you will likely have on hand in your fridge and pantry. The salad is creamy and has a nice tang from mustard and vinegar. Feel free to use more vegetables and add fresh herbs.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic dressing that I have made many times now. I never used vinegar or sugar before but it really gives blah old potato salad some zing. I used to throw out potato salad after a few days but I never have any leftover now. I never add the carrot or pimento or parsley and only add the celery when I have it. I have though, taken to mixing this dressing in a small bowl beforehand. I have always had a bit of a time, either making my potato cubes too hard, undercooked, or too mushy and they mash up too much when trying to blend in the dressing ingredients. Pre-mixing the dressing in the bowl, I can cook my potato cubes fairly soft and then gently fold in the pre-made dressing only to toss the onions, celery and potato cubes and eggs togehther and just coat with the dressing. A perfect chunky potato salad!

I made this twice. First, as printed. Then, for the second time, I chopped the potatoes BEFORE boiling; this halved the cooking time and made chopping easier. I also used red potatoes, so I didn't have to peel (but if I used Russets, I would have peeled them before chopping and boiling). I eliminated the celery (my family and I just don't like it in potato salad) and substituted 1/2 teaspoon celery salt (of course, I eliminated the regular salt). I doubled the pimento to counter the sweetness of the relish.

Added dill instead of parsley. Reduced to 3 tsp sugar . Mixed dressing first with carrots and chopped celery. Added in 10 min pressure cooker potatoes. Chopped into medium cubes. Will reduce mustard by half next time. Used red wine vinegar instead of white. Was really good and would be great with boiled eggs too.

A little bland. I add more onion and celer y, finely chopped red pepper, a small amount of grated sharp cheese. I always cube my potatoes before cooking and cook most of the onion and celery with them. I use just a little raw for crunch. I top it
with a scattering of green onions and a good sprinkle of paprika. I like eggs finely chopped as I hate chunks of egg white!

I used half dry mustard, half Dijon. I used Yukon gold potatoes, and put the vinegar on while potatoes were still warm, as suggested by another reviewer. I added some celery salt plus minced celery, and also put some dill weed in it (love dill!). This potato salad was a huge hit!

4 stars for recipe as is, though I had a few problems with this.
I've never boiled potatoes before and Doing this right is critical. This recipe calls for you to boil water then add whole potatoes, cool and chop after. This will result in mushy outside cooked and hard inside. I had to start all over again but instead, peeled and cut potatoes into 1/2 inch-1inch cubes, put them in cold water and brought that to a boil covered. Once boiling I uncovered and checked for doneness every 1-2 minutes by biting into pieces and cutting with a fork.

I was worried there was too much sugar so I decreased that by a third. I felt there was hardly any ingredients in this so I Added extra onion and carrot, probably double the original recipe. And lots lots more celery since I like it crunchy. I recommend mixing dressing first then folding into potatoe to prevent mushing them too much. It came out awesome and everyone loved it.
Of note--I made 3x the amount called for one recipe and of course tripled the ingredients but still felt like it was hardly enough though it would have still been good.

Super easy.
I chopped the potatoes before boiling (just because it's how i've always done it).
Took advice from other reviewers and mixed the dressing before adding to the potatoes.
I also added 5 chopped up hard boiled eggs to my potatoes before adding the dressing.
I subbed 2tsp onion powder for the onions (my kids won't eat onions)and also added 2 tsp of chia seeds and approx 5 tsp of grated carrots however i think i'll double this next time too.
I left out sugar, mustard, pimento, vinegar & relish as they are not to our tastes although i do think i may try adding mustard next time!
Can't wait for supper am sure it'll go down well it looks great!

This recipe was really yummy! I needed a potato salad recipe that didn't call for any eggs because I didn't have in the fridge at the time. I normally am not a big potato salad fan because I'm not a big fan of mayo, but the dressing in this salad didn't taste all that "mayonnaissy" to my delight. I followed the recipe as listed except I left out the celery and pimento because I didn't have any on hand. Also, instead of using pickle relish, I used some of my grandma's homemade pickles and just diced them up a bit. I think it may have been the pickles that made the dish, but regardless it was extremely tasty and went quick at our picnic. Oh yeah... one last alteration to the recipe... instead of peeling and boiling the potatoes, I kept the skins on and baked them in the microwave until done. Then I cut them in half and let them cool, and even stuck them in the freezer for about 30 minutes to harden a bit so that they didn't fall apart when I added them to the dressing. That seemed to work like a charm. The shredded carrots in it were a good addition to the salad too. Enjoy!

This recipe is great because you can make it to suit your/your families' tastes. Did not add onions, celery, pimento or carrots so the kids would like it. (In my opinion the carrots just give it color anyway) Was out of eggs, but would definitely add next time. I would have added celery seed instead of celery, but forgot; would add next time. And I would double or come close to doubling the relish next time. Oh, and I just used plain white vinegar instead of the white wine vinegar and it was not overpowering at all. I used olive oil mayo, which probably makes little difference. I had to add another 2 min to the cooking time of the potatoes even after I had cut them down to be equal size. I used Yukon gold potatoes and left some of the skin on. And I used the "make the dressing first" technique that other reviewers suggested, and then tossed the potatoes in. I served it with turkey burgers and corn on the cob for dinner and I'm ashamed to say I went back twice later that night for my "snack"!

I've never been great at making potato salad but my daughter requested some for our grandsons birthday party. After reviewing several recipes I decided to try this version. It was a huge success! People went back for seconds and thirds. I doubled the recipe and added 5 hard boiled eggs an eliminated the celery. I made the sauce the night before and added the eggs and potatoes the day of the party. Many people in our family like warm potato salad versus cold. The sauce is FABULOUS! This recipe is a keeper! My daughter called for the recipe on her way home so she could make it the next day

This was a little time consuming for me since I minced sweet pickles, red bell pepper, celery, and onion to make the potato salad, but it was well worth it. It tastes just like it comes from the restaurant, or even better!
Excellent recipe. I never add pimentos and it tastes great without it. I add extra onions and celery since a teaspoon is nothing really. I also cut back on the mayo as I find it a bit too much.

This was a huge hit at the Superbowl party. The only changes I made were to use onion powder and celery salt in very small amounts and to add more pimentos in place of the carrots. This was only because I was rushing at the time. Really delicious and everyone loved it.
It was yummy!
Love this recipe !!
Dressing to potato ratio was too high. Cut the mayo in half and double the vegetables.
Very tasty!
peal the potatoes

Great recipe. I’ve never had much luck making potato salad and it never had the proper zing. The first time I made the salad I made it according to the recipe only leaving out the pimento and carrots since I didn’t have any. It was a great hit. I’ve made it three more times since then changing nothing. Finally a potato salad that I make that tastes good!
This potato salad is awesome! I’d been making for numerous of times. Think I should shout out tp
